subject: joint ordinal/continuous factor model in lavaan and OpenMx

messages.author: 6db62e08ec862130
messages.subject: joint ordinal/continuous factor model in lavaan and OpenMx
parts:
I'm trying to understand how to specify the same model in lavaan and OpenMx.

A single factor model has 1 ordinal and 3 continuous indicators. Data is simulated. The variance of the factor is fixed to 1.0. The mean and variance of the ordinal indicator are fixed to 0 and 1, respectively (delta parameterization, I think).

This results in a 12 parameter model in OpenMx and 10 parameters in lavaan. I suspect lavaan omits the 2 thresholds when counting parameters?

When I run the attached code, most of the parameters are nearly the same, but the loading from the latent to the ordinal indicator is pretty far off.

Is the model the same? If not, how to diagnose the difference? If so, why is the ordinal loading so different? Which software is correct?

Thank you.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: joint ordinal/continuous factor model in lavaan and OpenMx
parts:
On 09/11/2017 04:32 PM, Joshua Pritikin wrote:
> A single factor model has 1 ordinal and 3 continuous indicators. Data is
> simulated. The variance of the factor is fixed to 1.0. The mean and
> variance of the ordinal indicator are fixed to 0 and 1, respectively
> (delta parameterization, I think).

> This results in a 12 parameter model in OpenMx and 10 parameters in
> lavaan. I suspect lavaan omits the 2 thresholds when counting parameters?

I see you are using the lavaan() function. This function fixes all
parameters to zero (or other fixed values), unless it is specified in
the model syntax. Therefore, thresholds are not estimated. You need to
either add them to the model syntax:

la.model <- '
G =~ o1 + c1 + c2 + c3
o1 | th1 + th2
'

or add the auto.th = TRUE argument to the lavaan() function call:

fit <- lavaan(la.model, data=j2$data$observed, estimator='DWLS',
auto.var=TRUE, std.lv=TRUE, int.ov.free=TRUE,
auto.th=TRUE,
auto.cov.lv.x=TRUE, parameterization="delta")

or you can simply use the sem() function, which usually comes with
reasonable defaults:

fit <- sem(la.model, data=j2$data$observed, std.lv = TRUE)

In this case, the point estimates are much closer, although still
somewhat different

> Which software is correct?
